id_and_class.summary: Graham Harman treats human consciousness as one kind of relation between objects, with no privileged place in reality. All objects, minds included, withdraw from one another and never fully grasp each other, so conscious experience engages only the ‘sensual’ profiles of things while real objects stay veiled.
id_and_class.core_identity_tagline: Consciousness as One Object Relation Among Many

conceptual_ground.explanatory_identity_claim: Consciousness is a type of interaction among objects: an intentional relation in which one object encounters the sensual object and sensual qualities of another, never the real object itself.
conceptual_ground.mind_body_relationship: Minds are objects among other objects. Harman denies that human awareness is the model for all relations, any more than fire, cotton, or granite are.
conceptual_ground.subjectivity_and_intentionality: Intentional objects, the things we encounter in thought and experience, are real but differ from the real objects behind them. Intentionality forms a differentiated network of relations between individual objects rather than one unified field.
conceptual_ground.qualia_account: Experiential qualities are sensual qualities: the profile an object presents in an encounter, as distinct from its real qualities.
conceptual_ground.ontological_commitments: Objects of every kind, each with a fourfold structure: real object, sensual object, real qualities, and sensual qualities.
conceptual_ground.epistemic_access: Access is always partial. Since being precedes access, Harman holds that philosophy should start from objects rather than from consciousness.
conceptual_ground.constituents_and_structure: The fourfold of real and sensual objects and real and sensual qualities. Consciousness operates on the sensual side.

mechanism_and_dynamics.scope_of_consciousness: Intentionality; perception; the place of consciousness in general ontology
mechanism_and_dynamics.distinctive_mechanism_or_principle: Withdrawal: no object, conscious or not, ever fully encounters or exhausts another, so every relation, including awareness, is partial and indirect.
mechanism_and_dynamics.location_and_distribution: Consciousness is one relation within a flat ontology in which all objects stand on equal footing.
mechanism_and_dynamics.information_flow_or_representation: The intentional object works like a translation or model of the real object: it interacts with us but does not give us the thing itself.
core_claims_and_evidence: The human-world relation is one relation among many and has no privileged ontological status.
All objects withdraw from each other, and the human mind cannot exhaust the objects it thinks about.
Conscious perception of a hammer meets a sensual hammer with a certain profile, not the hammer in itself.
Being precedes access, so objects exist and relate to each other beyond human awareness.

empirics_and_critiques.criticisms_and_tensions: If no object can fully access another, it is unclear how meaningful relations, including conscious ones, occur at all.
empirics_and_critiques.open_questions_and_limitations: Harman places consciousness within a general theory of objects but does not explain what distinguishes conscious relations from non-conscious ones, such as fire burning cotton.
empirics_and_critiques.ontological_coherence: Consistent within its flat ontology, which applies the same structure to every object. Its fit with a materialist classification is loose, since the theory concerns objects of any kind rather than matter.

sources_and_references.title_with_names: Harman’s Object-Oriented Ontology, Landscape of Consciousness, Robert Lawrence Kuhn
